account:
It is just after eight on day 1, and I am in my office with the secretary nearby. Today I have the ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, office hours at sixteen-thirty, and the innkeeper's confirmed meeting in the great hall at eighteen sharp. I have read and returned both appointment books.

I suspect some coordination in town that I do not yet understand. Yesterday the innkeeper invited the builder to the inn for a private supplies discussion. The secretary told me freight was seeking the miller and builder to coordinate warehouse supplies. There were also reports of the baker carrying a sack of bread near the plaza, and I myself saw freight carrying a bread sack near town hall. My neighbour relayed Townsfolk 02's report of lights or decorations at the bakery, but had not confirmed it; the baker reportedly knew of no special occasion. These could be ordinary supplies and baking business, or preparations for some gathering, but I have no firm evidence of an event or its purpose.

The innkeeper specifically requested tomorrow's meeting yesterday, confirmed eighteen sharp in the great hall, and told me no preparation was needed. That appointment might explain the activity, but he described it only as an inn business matter, so I cannot assume a connection. I heard him speaking and shouting this morning without making out the words. The secretary has reported no danger or public damage. The town accounts were not found on the great hall tables yesterday; I do not know where they are or whether that has any connection. I intend to keep my appointments and learn more through ordinary conversations rather than treat these uncertain reports as facts.
